additional_info.subject: Note to L3
additional_info.body:
Suspected Root Cause
: NA
Problem Description
: coap error polling was observed 54 times over the past 4 weeks on DC2 outlet.
Action Performed (L2)
: We analyzed the logs based on the timestamps provided by the customer and found that the coap error caused the outlet to go "out of order" for a few seconds, after which the outlet returned to a healthy state.
Charger SW Version
: v6.1.3
Reason for Handover (L3)
: Further investigation is required, and if possible, an update to EcoG v1.4.11 should be considered.
Log Analysis with Timestamp
: Logs corresponding to the provided customer timestamp are attached in the note.
Action Required by HQ
: A deeper investigation is needed, and if feasible, an update to EcoG v1.4.11 should be applied.
Attachment
: Screenshot of the AWS coap error is attached in the note.

additional_info.subject: 0417721 - ID0417631-DC/Si-D/AT-[MP / S3 170003317] SECC- error code (C1) CRM:00314000159
additional_info.body:
Good afternoon Lara,
My name is Fosco, I am reaching out from the Expert Services team in regards of child case
0417721
. The ticket was opened to explain the new error messages observed on your end.
First of all, everything is working as intended. With the latest FW version of Sicharge D v6.1.3,
new OCPP Vender Error Codes were introduced
. These vendor codes are intended to provide more information to the Backend in terms of charger's behavior, but they are not referring to new errors per se. The charger has been experiencing these loss of communications also before, simply they were not reported to the Backend.
In details, as already explained by my colleague Sominath:
The VendorErrorCode “
modbus0 is not connected
” refers to a loss of communication to the SECC for 750ms. This event has no impact on the performance of the charger, even during a charging session. Only in rare case it could lead to outlets being unavailable for several seconds or interrupt a charging session.
The VendorErrorCode “
secc is offline
” refers to the happening of the coap polling error, an internal communication to SECC lost for a small interval of time. The OpenController will reconnect to the SECC within 5 seconds. Also in this case, this event has no impact on the charger, even during charging session.
In case these errors appear more and more often, we could install a Hotfix on the SECC of the charger, which includes hardening patches regarding Coap communication and a Modbus reconnection hardening.
Furthermore, R&D team is planning, for the next FW release, to reduce the spamming of these error messages when they have no effect on the charger in terms of outlet unavailability.
As explained above, these are not new errors introduced by the new FW v6.1.3, but just new messages sent to the Backend. Unfortunately, we missed a proper communication to the CPOs in regards of the introduction of these new error messages. We apologize for that and we will communicate future new vendor codes within the Release Notes and Software Manual.
In case you have further questions, please do not hesitate to reply to this email.
Looking forward to hearing your feedback soon.
